x: Cows say moo, and they give us milk.
Birds fly with their wings.
Fish breathe in water with their gills.
Frogs have long strong back legs for jumping.
Bees make honey from the sweet juice of flowers.
Cats have four legs and a tail, but no wings.

q: How many legs does a dog have?
x: Dogs walk on four legs.
Birds build nests from twigs and grass.

q: A baby cat is called a kitten.
x: Baby cats are kittens and baby dogs are puppies.
Elephants are the biggest animals that live on land.
Ducks have webbed feet that work like paddles.
Hens lay eggs. Chicks hatch out of them.
Snakes have no legs. They slide on their bellies.
Cows eat grass all day long.

q: Which animal has a long trunk?
x: An elephant uses its trunk like a hand and a straw.
Bats hang upside down by their feet to sleep.
A caterpillar makes a cocoon, then comes out as a butterfly!
Whales live in the sea but they breathe air, like us. They are mammals.

q: How many legs does a spider have?
x: Spiders have 8 legs. Insects have 6.
Penguins cannot fly, but they are amazing swimmers.

q: Which animal is the fastest runner?
x: A cheetah can run as fast as a car on the highway.

q: A frog starts life as a tadpole.
x: Tadpoles live in water and slowly grow legs.
Many bears sleep through the cold winter. This is called hibernation.
Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, and that helps fruit grow.
Sharks swim in the sea. They have been around longer than dinosaurs!

q: A giraffe has a very short neck.
x: Giraffes have the longest necks of all animals, to reach high leaves.
Ants are insects: six legs and three body parts.
Octo means eight. An octopus has eight arms and three hearts!
We see with our eyes and hear with our ears.
Our ears catch sounds.

q: We should wash our hands before we eat.
x: Washing with soap takes the germs away.

q: How many fingers are on one hand?
x: Five fingers on each hand: ten in all!
Your body grows and rests while you sleep.
Our nose smells flowers, cake and everything else.
Brush in the morning and before bed.

q: Which food is good for you?
x: Fruit and vegetables help your body stay strong.
Your heart is a strong muscle that pumps blood all day and night.
Lungs take in air when we breathe in.

q: Babies have more bones than grown-ups.
x: Babies have about 300 bones. Some join together as they grow, so adults have 206.
Your brain thinks, remembers and tells your body what to do.

q: Drinking water is good for your body.
x: More than half of your body is water!

q: How many teeth does a grown-up have?
x: Children have 20 baby teeth; grown-ups have 32.

q: What do plants need to grow?
x: Plants need water, sunlight and soil.
Roots hold the tree in the ground and drink water.
Leaves are green because of a helper called chlorophyll.
Apples grow on apple trees, from flowers in spring.
In autumn many leaves turn yellow, orange and red, then fall.
A tiny seed in the soil can grow into a big flower.
Winter is the coldest season. Sometimes it snows!
When water gets very cold, it turns into ice.

q: What do bees take from flowers?
x: Bees drink nectar from flowers and turn it into honey.

q: Plants make their own food from sunlight.
x: Leaves use sunlight, air and water to make food. This is called photosynthesis.

q: Which tree stays green all winter?
x: Pine trees keep their needles all year long.

q: A cactus needs lots of rain.
x: Cactuses live in deserts and store water inside.

q: What is a forest full of?
x: Forests are full of trees, and many animals live there.
Mushrooms are not plants. They are fungi.
Clouds are made of tiny drops. When they get heavy, they fall as rain.
The Sun is a giant hot star. It warms the Earth.

q: What do we see after rain and sun?
x: Sunlight shining through raindrops makes a rainbow.

q: We can see stars at night.
x: Stars are there in the day too, but the Sun is too bright to see them.

q: What do we wear when it rains?
x: A raincoat and boots keep us dry.
Snow is very cold. It is made of tiny pieces of ice.

q: What shines in the sky in the day?
x: The Sun gives us daylight.
Wind pushes the clouds across the sky.
Light is faster than sound, so we see lightning before we hear thunder.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
Fog is a cloud that sits close to the ground.
Snowflakes have six arms, and no two look exactly the same.
Winter, spring, summer, autumn - and around again.

q: The Sun goes around the Earth.
x: The Earth goes around the Sun. It takes one year.

q: Who goes to space in a rocket?
x: Astronauts travel to space in rockets.
Earth is our home planet, with land, sea and air.
Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock.

q: The Moon is shaped like a ball.
x: The Moon is round like a ball. We just see different parts of it lit up.
Mars is called the red planet because of its red dust.

q: You can breathe on the Moon without a helmet.
x: There is no air on the Moon, so astronauts wear space suits.
Jupiter is so big that more than 1000 Earths could fit inside.
The Sun is our closest star. Other stars are much farther away.

q: How many planets go around our Sun?
x: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

q: Our galaxy is called the Milky Way.
x: The Milky Way has billions of stars. Our Sun is one of them.

q: What do we look at stars with?
x: A telescope makes faraway things look big and close.

q: The Moon makes its own light.
x: The Moon shines because sunlight bounces off it.

q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
x: Mercury is closest to the Sun, and Neptune is the farthest.

q: A satellite goes around the Earth.
x: Satellites help with phones, TV, maps and weather.

q: What is the sea full of?
x: Seas and oceans are full of salty water.
Sea water has salt in it, so we should not drink it.

q: Where is it very hot and sandy?
x: Deserts are dry, sandy and often very hot.
Some mountains are so tall that they have snow on top all year.
Oceans are the biggest bodies of water. They cover most of the Earth.

q: Most of the Earth is covered by water.
x: About seven tenths of the Earth is ocean.

q: What comes out of a volcano?
x: Lava is melted rock, so hot that it glows.

q: The Earth spins around once every day.
x: When our side faces the Sun it is day; when it turns away it is night.

q: Where is it always very cold?
x: The North and South Poles are covered in ice.
Most rivers start in the mountains and end in the sea.
Bananas are fruit. They grow in bunches.
Cows, goats and sheep give milk.
Ripe bananas are yellow.
We eat the carrot root that grows in the soil.

q: What do we make bread from?
x: Flour is made from wheat, and bread is baked from flour.
Hens lay the eggs we eat.
Corn kernels pop when they get hot.
Tomatoes have seeds inside, so they are fruit, even though we use them like vegetables.
Cheese is made from milk.

q: Honey can stay good for a very long time.
x: Honey does not go bad. Bees made it to keep for winter.

q: How many sides does a triangle have?
x: Tri means three: a triangle has 3 sides.
A circle is round, like a ball or a plate.
Two and one more make three.
A square has four sides, all the same length.
7 is bigger than 3.
Five and five make ten - like your two hands!

q: How many days are in a week?
x: Seven days: Monday to Sunday.
Take 3 away from 10 and 7 are left.
Hexa means six. Bees build hexagons in their hives!
Even numbers can be shared into two equal groups: 2, 4, 6, 8...

q: How many minutes are in an hour?
x: An hour has 60 minutes.
Three twice: 3 + 3 = 6.
A sphere is perfectly round in every direction.
Cat - C, A, T.
Ship - S, H, I, P.
Key - K, E, Y.
Ball starts with the sound b.

q: What is the opposite of hot?
x: Hot and cold are opposites.

q: What is the opposite of up?
x: Up and down are opposites.
Cat and hat both end with -at.

q: How many letters are in DOG?
x: D, O, G: three letters.
Red means stop, green means go.

q: We look both ways before crossing the road.
x: Look left, look right, and hold a grown-up's hand.

q: Who helps when we are sick?
x: Doctors and nurses help us get better.
Sharing makes playing more fun for everyone.
A pilot flies the plane.
Old paper can be made into new paper. That saves trees!

q: What do we use to tell the time?
x: A clock or a watch tells us the time.

q: Nowruz is the Persian New Year, on the first day of spring.
x: Nowruz means new day. Families set the Haft-sin table.

q: What does a magnet pick up?
x: Magnets pull things made of iron, like nails.

q: Ice melts when it gets warm.
x: Warm ice turns back into water.
Boats float. Rocks and keys sink.
Without light, everything looks dark.

q: What happens to water when it boils?
x: Boiling water turns into steam.
Whales and dolphins talk to each other with sounds under water.
When something blocks the light, it makes a shadow behind it.
Without air in the way, a feather and a hammer fall together. Astronauts tried it on the Moon!
